claim: dotenv-checker (tanguykonan) recursively scans a workspace for .env files and detects missing, empty, and undocumented keys against .env.example reference templates, plus env-vs-env diffs.
quote: It detects missing, empty, and undocumented keys across your environment files and reference templates, with built-in tools to synchronize them safely. ... Diffs environments directly (such as staging against production)
title: dotenv-checker

claim: dotenv-checker can auto-fix (--fix) with --dry-run and --backup, emits --json, exits 0/1 for CI, and never overwrites existing keys, values or comments on sync.
quote: Existing keys, local values, and custom comments are never overwritten.
title: dotenv-checker

claim: envaudit splits findings into errors (missing vars, possible secrets leaked into .env.example, unquoted values with spaces) vs warnings (undocumented vars, empty values).
quote: Errors: Missing variables, possible secrets in .env.example, unquoted values with spaces. Warnings: Undocumented variables, empty values
title: envaudit

claim: envaudit masks secret-looking values in diff output and can generate markdown env docs grouped by prefix (Variable, Required, Default, Group).
quote: Shows keys only in each file and keys with different values. Secret-looking values are masked. ... Outputs a table grouped by prefix (DB_, APP_, AWS_, etc.) with columns: Variable, Required, Default, Group.
title: envaudit

claim: dotenv-linter (Rust) runs 14 syntax/style checks — duplicated key, lowercase key, unordered key, schema violation, quote/space characters, substitution key, trailing whitespace etc. — with check/fix/diff and auto-backup on fix.
quote: Duplicated key ... Schema violation ... Unordered key ... Value without quotes; Original file was backed up to: ".env_1601378896"
title: dotenv-linter

claim: envguard check diffs .env vs .env.example: missing or empty keys exit 1; undocumented keys are warnings only.
quote: `check` exits with code `1` for missing or empty keys. Undocumented keys produce warnings only and do not fail the check.
title: envguard

claim: envguard sync appends missing keys with empty values and never overwrites existing keys.
quote: Adds missing keys from `.env.example` into your `.env` with empty values. **Existing keys are never overwritten.**
title: envguard

claim: envguard audit walks git history (all local refs, merge commits) flagging committed .env files and secret-pattern lines (API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, Slack/GitHub/Stripe tokens); exits 1 on findings.
quote: Walks history reachable from all local refs, including merge commits, and flags committed `.env` files plus lines matching common secret patterns such as API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, Slack tokens, GitHub tokens, and Stripe keys.
title: envguard

claim: envguard scan-config extracts ${VAR} and ${VAR:default} placeholders from YAML/.properties config (Spring Boot, Quarkus) and --strict fails when required vars are absent from the env file — env requirements can be derived from app config, not just .env.example.
quote: Extracts `${VAR}` and `${VAR:default}` placeholders from YAML and `.properties` config files. Required variables (no default) and optional variables (with default) are reported separately.
title: envguard

claim: dotenv-sentinel checks three pillars — completeness vs .env.example or JSON schema, secret hygiene (weak/default secrets, real credentials in example files), and git exposure (tracked files, .gitignore coverage, history) — and always masks values.
quote: `dotenv-sentinel` finds every `.env`, `.env.*` and `*.env` file in a project and checks three things: **completeness** ... **secret hygiene** ... and **git exposure** ... **Values are never printed**: every secret is masked.
title: dotenv-sentinel

claim: dotenv-sentinel assigns severities per rule: committed-env and example-contains-secret are critical; known-secret, env-in-history, env-not-ignored, weak-secret, missing-var are high; type-mismatch/empty-required/short-secret/debug-in-production medium; insecure-url/unquoted-space/undefined-reference/extra-var low.
quote: committed-env | critical | .env file with real values is tracked by git; example-contains-secret | critical; env-in-history | high; weak-secret | high; missing-var | high; type-mismatch | medium; extra-var | low; missing-example | info
title: dotenv-sentinel

claim: dotenv-sentinel supports a JSON env schema with typed variables: string, number, integer, boolean, url, email, port, json, enum, plus pattern, minLength and secret flags.
quote: required, empty, type (`string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `url`, `email`, `port`, `json`, `enum`), `pattern`, `enum`, `minLength`, `secret`
title: dotenv-sentinel

claim: Template filename conventions recognized: .env.example, .env.sample, .env.template, .env.dist, <file>.example.
quote: (or `.env.sample`, `.env.template`, `.env.dist`, `<file>.example`, or `--example`)
title: dotenv-sentinel

claim: dotenv-sentinel's config file supports severity overrides and allow-list suppressions that require a reason and optional expiry; expired suppressions resurface as an allow-expired finding.
quote: Each entry needs a `rule` ... and a `reason` ... When `expires` (YYYY-MM-DD) has passed, the finding comes back together with an `allow-expired` finding, so exceptions can't be forgotten.
title: dotenv-sentinel

claim: Dominant env-validation pattern across all five tools: key-set diff of .env vs .env.example producing three finding classes — missing (error), undocumented/extra (warning), empty (warning) — plus optional fix/sync that never overwrites, machine-readable output (--json/SARIF), and exit codes for CI. Secret hygiene and git exposure are second-generation additions (envguard audit, dotenv-sentinel).
quote: synthesis of READMEs 50-54
title: multiple

claim: Vercel framework detection model: each preset has detectors {every, some} of items {path, matchContent, matchPackage}; matchPackage matches a package name inside package.json, matchContent is a regex on a file's full contents, path checks file existence; a fallback:true detector only wins when no non-fallback matches.
quote: path?: string; A file path to detect ... matchContent?: string; A matcher for the entire file ... matchPackage?: string; A matcher for a package specifically found in a "package.json" file ... fallback?: boolean; If true, this detector only wins when no non-fallback framework detector matches.
title: @vercel/frameworks types.ts

claim: Vercel presets ship suggested settings (installCommand/buildCommand/devCommand/outputDirectory) with value+UI placeholder, envPrefix (e.g. NEXT_PUBLIC_), sort ordering, supersedes slugs, and detectionConfidence weak|strong for incidental deps.
quote: detectionConfidence?: 'weak' | 'strong'; `weak` means the detection is commonly incidental (e.g. Storybook as a devDependency of an app that deploys something else)
title: @vercel/frameworks types.ts

claim: Next.js detection is a single matchPackage 'next'; its preset suggests devCommand 'next dev --port $PORT' and buildCommand 'next build'.
quote: detectors: { every: [ { matchPackage: 'next' } ] } ... devCommand: { value: 'next dev --port $PORT' }
title: @vercel/frameworks frameworks.ts

claim: Cross-language detection example — Vercel detects Django by content-matching requirements.txt, pyproject.toml or Pipfile for [Dd]jango, OR manage.py containing DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE; Python frameworks supersede the generic 'python' runtime preset.
quote: { path: 'requirements.txt', matchContent: '[Dd]jango' }, { path: 'pyproject.toml', matchContent: '[Dd]jango' }, { path: 'Pipfile', matchContent: '[Dd]jango' }, { path: 'manage.py', matchContent: 'DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE' }
title: @vercel/frameworks frameworks.ts

claim: Vercel notes the dependency detector must reference a CLI package, not a library — a Gatsby site can use Preact, so it detects preact-cli not preact.
quote: the `dependency` property needs to reference a CLI. ... you can't look for the `preact` dependency. Instead, you need to look for `preact-cli`
title: @vercel/frameworks frameworks.ts

claim: Netlify @netlify/framework-info detects via detect.npmDependencies + excludedNpmDependencies + configFiles per framework JSON, and returns dev commands, dev server port, TCP/HTTP readiness polling strategies, build directory, and env vars to set.
quote: dev: { commands: ['gatsby develop'], port: 8000, pollingStrategies: [{ name: 'TCP' }, { name: 'HTTP' }] }
location: README Add or update a framework
title: @netlify/framework-info

claim: Netlify excludedNpmDependencies is the inverse rule — presence of an excluded package disqualifies the framework match (handles meta-framework ambiguity).
quote: Inverse of `npmDependencies`. If any project is using one of those packages, it will not be considered as using the framework.
title: @netlify/framework-info

claim: Netlify build-info detects in layers: package manager, workspaces, build systems, frameworks, build settings — and takes baseDir + rootDir separately for monorepos.
quote: It provides a layered approach to detecting the following information: 1. Package Manager 2. Workspaces (pnpm, yarn, npm) 3. Build Systems 4. Frameworks 5. Build Settings
title: @netlify/build-info

claim: pier finds a project's root by walking up from the process cwd looking for marker files: package.json, .git, pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, Gemfile, go.mod, Cargo.toml, composer.json, deno.json/.jsonc, bun.lockb, mix.exs.
quote: static let markers = ["package.json", ".git", "pyproject.toml", "requirements.txt", "Gemfile", "go.mod", "Cargo.toml", "composer.json", "deno.json", "deno.jsonc", "bun.lockb", "mix.exs"]
title: pier IdentifyProject.swift

claim: pier's argv detection rules are ordered meta-frameworks before bundlers and runtimes last, first match wins — matching on argv token basenames (words) or full cmdline substrings (phrases), e.g. next-server, manage.py runserver, artisan serve, uvicorn, phx.server.
quote: /// Ordered: meta-frameworks before their bundlers, runtimes last. First match wins.
title: pier IdentifyProject.swift

claim: pier refines Vite detections: when argv says plain Vite it reads package.json deps and upgrades to SvelteKit/Remix/Nuxt/Astro (viteHosts); depRules also map deps to frameworks (next, nuxt, @sveltejs/kit, @remix-run/ prefix, @angular/core, @nestjs/core, fastify, express).
quote:
/// When argv says plain Vite but package.json reveals a meta-framework built on it.
    static let viteHosts: Set<String> = ["sveltekit", "remix", "nuxt", "astro"]
title: pier IdentifyProject.swift

claim: pier's infra detection: name match beats port match; separate dockerPorts list only applies when the process is docker/orbstack-proxied; port-only matches are skipped when the process otherwise looks like a dev server.
quote: /// Name match beats port match. Port-only matches are skipped for processes that look like someone's dev server (project cwd, JS/Python runtime, known framework), unless docker-proxied.
title: pier IdentifyInfra.swift

claim: pier resolves git branch by parsing .git/HEAD directly (no git subprocess), handling worktrees where .git is a gitdir: pointer file; detached HEAD yields a 7-char sha.
quote: Handles worktrees/submodules where `.git` is a file ("gitdir: …")
title: pier IdentifyProject.swift

claim: pier's identification pipeline combines: process cwd, process args, package.json, .git/HEAD, well-known infrastructure ports, Docker Engine API, and a quick HTTP probe for page title and favicon.
quote: **Identification** combines the process's working directory, its arguments, `package.json`, `.git/HEAD`, well-known infrastructure ports, the Docker Engine API and a quick HTTP probe for the page title and favicon.
title: pier README

claim: The neethanwu pier implementation uses lsof to find listening TCP ports then resolves process → working directory → project name → git branch, polling every 2 seconds with no daemons or privileged helpers.
quote: Pier uses `lsof` to detect listening TCP ports, then resolves each to a process → working directory → project name → git branch. It polls every 2 seconds and uses no background daemons or privileged helpers.
title: Pier (neethanwu)

claim: Portlivo's folder-to-commands convention table: Procfile.dev/Procfile (every line), composer.json dev script (composer run dev), artisan (php artisan serve + queue:work), package.json (dev/start/serve/watch via lockfile-matched npm/pnpm/yarn/bun), bin/dev or bin/rails, manage.py (runserver), go.mod (go run .), docker-compose.yml/compose.yaml (docker compose up, unticked).
quote: `package.json` | Its `dev`, `start`, `serve` or `watch` script, run with npm, pnpm, yarn or bun to match the lockfile ... `manage.py` | `python3 manage.py runserver` ... `go.mod` | `go run .`
title: Portlivo: Projects

claim: Portlivo priority rule: a Procfile wins over inferred commands because it lists exactly what the project runs.
quote: A Procfile wins: when there is one, it's what gets ticked, because it lists exactly what the project runs.
title: Portlivo: Projects

claim: Portlivo runs suggested commands in a login shell from the project folder so shell-profile PATH (nvm, Herd, Homebrew) applies — relevant for our env/spawn behavior.
quote: Each command runs in a login shell from the project folder, so the PATH from your shell profile (nvm, Herd, Homebrew) applies.
title: Portlivo: Projects

claim: Portlivo's 'Save as Project' captures commands already running from a folder with their exact arguments — detection from observed processes, not just files.
quote: Right-click any running server from the project and choose **Save as Project**. Every command running from that folder goes in, with its exact arguments.
title: Portlivo: Projects

claim: pier.yml is a local stack-file convention: services with run/cwd/port/env/depends_on/ready (http|port|log:regex|none); pier up orders into dependency waves, waits for readiness, and fails if a service's port is held by something else; discovered by walking up from cwd to $HOME for pier.yml/pier.yaml/.pier.yml/.pier.yaml.
quote: `pier up` / `pier down` look for `pier.yml`, `pier.yaml`, `.pier.yml` or `.pier.yaml` in the current directory and then in each parent directory, stopping at `$HOME`. ... `ready` | How to know it is up. Default: `port` if `port` is set, else `none`.
title: pier.yml: stack files

claim: Scan-worthy project conventions synthesized for our scanner: package.json (scripts + dep names, lockfile for pm), pyproject.toml/requirements.txt/Pipfile (content-match deps), manage.py (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE), go.mod, Cargo.toml, composer.json+artisan, Gemfile+bin/rails|bin/dev, deno.json, mix.exs, Procfile/Procfile.dev (authoritative multi-command), docker-compose.yml/compose.yaml, .git (root+branch), Makefile (not covered by pier/Portlivo — gap worth adding ourselves).
quote: synthesis of pier markers + Portlivo table + Vercel detectors
title: multiple

claim: Dashboard mapping suggestion for env surface: scan project dirs for .env + template alternates; surface missing keys as issues, undocumented as warnings; mask secret values; offer 'sync missing keys' action; optionally check .gitignore coverage of .env (env-not-ignored is the highest-value cheap check). Schema types and git-history audit are overkill for v1.
quote: synthesis of tools' feature split: all five diff keys; only envguard/sentinel do git history; only sentinel does schema types
title: multiple

claim: Process-to-stack attribution heuristic to adopt: name match beats port match; meta-frameworks before bundlers; argv-first then package.json deps to disambiguate Vite; skip port-only infra labeling when the process has dev context (project cwd, runtime, known framework).
quote: from pier IdentifyProject/IdentifyInfra rule ordering comments
title: pier
